trigger.message: Skill 'aiml-access-diagnostics' was NOT triggered (no skills were loaded)

expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output requires the agent to actually perform the diagnosis: render a hop-by-hop authorization chain, identify that cross-region inference profiles (us. prefix) require permissions on BOTH the profile ARN and the underlying foundation-model ARN in each destination region, and note that an SCP blocking any single destination region would fail the whole request. This is a well-known Bedrock pattern that the agent should have been able to diagnose directly from the problem description (caller has InvokeModel on the inference-profile ARN only, which is the classic missing-foundation-model-ARN gap for cross-region inference profiles).

Instead, the agent's response is entirely a clarifying-question response — it declines to produce any diagnosis and asks for account ID, region, role ARN, profile ARN, and how the role is assumed. While it does mention in passing that 'cross-region inference profiles route to underlying regional model ARNs, and a policy that only covers the profile ARN... is a common culprit here' — this is a one-line hint buried in a question, not a structured hop-by-hop diagnosis. It does not render the authorization chain, does not explicitly state the fix (grant permission on both profile ARN and foundation-model ARN in every destination region), and does not mention the SCP-blocking-one-region implication at all.

The response fails to meet the 'not just prose' requirement in the opposite direction — it's not even prose diagnosis, it's clarifying questions. The core expected content (hop-by-hop chain, specific gap identification, SCP note) is essentially absent.
expected_output.evidence: "To trace this properly I'll need a few specifics before I can walk the chain... Once I have those I'll trace caller identity → role trust policy → role permission policies → resource policy (if any) → SCPs/RCPs → the underlying regional model ARN(s) the profile resolves to, and name the exact hop that's denying."

assertion_results.text: Presents the diagnosis as a hop-by-hop authorization chain with an explicit verdict per hop, not only prose advice
assertion_results.evidence: The agent's response consists entirely of a request for clarifying information (account ID, region, role ARN, inference profile ARN, assumption method) and ends with a plan: 'Once I have those I'll trace caller identity → role trust policy → role permission policies → resource policy (if any) → SCPs/RCPs → the underlying regional model ARN(s)...' with no actual verdicts given per hop.
assertion_results.reasoning: The output does not present any hop-by-hop diagnosis with verdicts; it only outlines what it will do once given more information. There is no structured diagnosis delivered, only a plan and a request for inputs.

assertion_results.text: Identifies the missing underlying foundation-model ARN grant (across every destination region the profile routes to) as the cause, not the profile grant
assertion_results.evidence: The agent only hints at this as a possibility in prose: 'a policy that only covers the profile ARN (not the regional model ARNs it fans out to) is a common culprit here' but does not identify this as THE cause of the specific issue described, nor does it confirm it across every destination region.
assertion_results.reasoning: The assertion requires the output to identify the missing underlying foundation-model ARN grant across every destination region as the cause. The agent only speculates this is a 'common culprit' in general, not asserting it as the specific diagnosis for this case, and does not mention 'every destination region' explicitly as needing grants.

assertion_results.text: Notes that an SCP denying any single destination region fails the entire Converse request
assertion_results.evidence: There is no mention of SCPs denying a single destination region causing the entire Converse request to fail. The only mention of SCPs is in the planned chain: '→ SCPs/RCPs → the underlying regional model ARN(s)' with no explanation of behavior.
assertion_results.reasoning: The output does not discuss SCP behavior or its effect on the Converse request at all beyond listing it as a step to check in the future plan.
